interpretation: Reference weights alter only the utility objective. Exact all-augmented-sample risk constraints remain unchanged.
For p_H=.1 the global utility optimum reallocates risk budget and raises expected utility by 0.07875 over equal-share.
The improvement is not pointwise: the (0,2) state receives a lower action while the (1,1) state receives a higher, more conservative action.
For p_H=.5,.8,.9 this example has no objective gain over equal-share.
The distribution-free maximin objective obtains worst-state utility 0.5 and does not share the skewed-reference gain.
limitations: Two-type synthetic example only; utility is a linear proxy, not CIFAR specificity.
Weights must be fixed before calibration or learned from independent data unless an additional adaptation proof is supplied.
Global optimization is exact only for the specified finite state space, linear risk family and chosen utility objective.
This is a new optimizer, not a replacement for all recertification theorems and not a SOTA result.
